overlaps.locator: Results → “Estimating fitness of evolutionary-relevant genotypes,” printed article pp. 3–5; Supplementary Information S2 → “Table1 property of segments”
overlaps.quote: “Across 11 experiments, we measured fitness for a total of 4,018,105 genotypes (875,151 unique amino acid sequences) with high accuracy. Of these, 422,717 consist solely of combinations of extant amino acid states from His3 orthologues”; “55,296 genotypes out of which we determined the fitness for 48,198, or 87%”; Table1 column “Number of unique amino acid sequences with measured fitness” cells “125915”; “122167”; “94031”; “69050”; “99891”; “83625”; “26364”; “73781”; “81497”; “79905”; “37167”; “63255”; “956648”; “875151”; Table1 column “Number of unique amino acid sequences containing only extant amino acids” cells “58066”; “45657”; “48198”; “44255”; “51122”; “45280”; “4313”; “46307”; “29992”; “29837”; “16763”; “32919”; “452709”; “422717”.
overlaps.definition_quote: “For each segment we measured fitness for 60% - 99.8% of all possible genotypes from the combinatorial set of selected extant amino acid states found in 21 yeast species”; “For segment 3 … we determined the fitness for 48,198, or 87% of the possible yeast extant states combinations in our library.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper reports unique measured sequences and a separate extant-state subset from an incomplete combinatorial sample. GraphFLA n_configs is the count of vertices retained after graph construction and isolate pruning. In addition, the raw GEO AAseq strings are variable length; a direct SequenceLandscape build cannot construct the graph without an alignment/encoding step not applied here.

input.preprocessing: Attempted the archived S03 AAseq and s columns as supplied; no padding, alignment, row filtering, or fitness transformation.

overlaps.reason: The direct S03 build failed before graph construction with ValueError: All sequences must have the same length (expected 25, got 27 for sequence 3). Because a segment graph could not be built from the unaltered processed sequences, no n_configs value is reported.

overlaps.locator: Supplementary Information S2 → “Table1 property of segments”; Results → “Estimating fitness of evolutionary-relevant genotypes,” printed article p. 3
overlaps.definition_quote: “We merged nucleotide genotypes that correspond to the same amino acid sequence and summed their frequencies and variances.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: These are nucleotide-level unique sequence counts from the supplementary table. The paper’s principal landscapes and GraphFLA protein-class comparison operate on amino-acid genotypes; the processed GEO files preserve AAseq and s rather than the per-nucleotide genotype strings needed for DNALandscape.

input.preprocessing: No nucleotide-level genotype-fitness table was reconstructed from the available processed AAseq tables.

overlaps.reason: The publisher S2 workbook supplies counts but not nucleotide genotype rows; the downloaded GEO processed tables are amino-acid sequence data. The DNA landscape cannot be rebuilt from those tables.

overlaps.locator: Results → “Ruggedness and multidimensional epistasis of the His3 fitness landscape,” printed article p. 10; Methods → “Quantifying sign epistasis,” pp. 23–24
overlaps.quote: “We found that 86 out of 128 (67%) sites in our library exhibit sign epistasis and 46% (59/128) exhibit reciprocal sign epistasis with 8% (968/11597) of all pairs of sites exhibiting sign epistasis.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “For each amino acid replacement … we considered only those that exhibit a large fitness effect (abs. difference > 0.4)”; “we identified secondary amino acid replacements that significantly alter the ratio of large increases to large decreases in fitness (Fisher’s exact test, Bonferroni corrected p-value < 0.05)”; “We only consider a site to be under sign epistasis if there is a second site that alters the frequency of sign epistasis in a statistically significant manner.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper classifies amino-acid sites and site pairs using fitness effects across genetic backgrounds, a >0.4 threshold, and a multiple-tested Fisher test. GraphFLA classify_epistasis returns motif-class proportions over four-node graph motifs. Units, filtering rule, and denominators differ.

input.preprocessing: Table 5 supplies the sign-epistasis pair summary; no graph-based motif analysis was run.

overlaps.graphfla_call: not run; motif fractions and paper site-level classifications are definition-incompatible
overlaps.reason: The article’s percentages are not proportions among GraphFLA four-node motifs.

overlaps.locator: Results → “Unidimensional epistasis of the His3 fitness landscape,” printed article p. 7; Methods → “Predicting fitness using deep learning,” pp. 22–23
overlaps.quote: “The ability of the cliff-like threshold fitness function to predict fitness from genotype varied between the His3 segments from near perfect (r² = 0.97) in segment 7, to relatively poor (r² = 0.44) in segment 5.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “The single neuron of the first layer computes the fitness potential, which is then mapped to a fitness value obtained from f(p), the function of the fitness potential which is found by the three layers of the neural network architecture.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper reports prediction R² from a deep neural network with a nonlinear sigmoid/threshold function of a latent fitness potential. GraphFLA higher_order_epistasis is polynomial regression by interaction order.

input.preprocessing: Paper R² values refer to segments 7 and 5; both processed inputs were acquired. No graph build or alternative regression was run.

overlaps.reason: The R² values describe a different fitted model and cannot be reproduced by GraphFLA higher_order_epistasis without changing the target definition.

overlaps.locator: Results → “Estimating fitness of evolutionary-relevant genotypes,” printed article p. 6
overlaps.quote: “Remarkably, 85% (330/389) of replacements between extant amino acid states had substantially different effects on fitness in different backgrounds.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “Among them we counted those with strong fitness effects, including deleterious mutations when the fitness effect was < -0.4 and beneficial when the fitness effect was > 0.4. We concluded that a particular amino acid replacement exhibits a strong deleterious or beneficial effect in some background if the fraction of such backgrounds exceeded the false discovery rate.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper’s quantity is background dependence of amino-acid replacement effects under its neutral/strong-effect procedure. GraphFLA evolvability_enhancing_mutations is under review, so definition equivalence is unknown.

input.preprocessing: Paper cumulative analysis excludes segment 9; all eleven remaining processed segment files are available. No GraphFLA run because the metric is under review.

overlaps.reason: The metric is under review and no definition-compatible result is asserted.

overlaps.locator: Supporting Information → S2 Fig caption, “Sequencing strategy and accuracy analysis of His3 segment libraries”
overlaps.quote: “99.63% of nonsense genotypes have a fitness > 0.4 while 23.46% of extant amino acid combinations have fitness < 0.6.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “99.63% of nonsense genotypes have a fitness > 0.4 while 23.46% of extant amino acid combinations have fitness < 0.6.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: These are thresholded fractions of two genotype categories, while GraphFLA fitness_distribution returns unitless shape statistics such as skewness, kurtosis, and CV.

input.preprocessing: Publisher S2 figure reports aggregate threshold fractions; all twelve processed segment files are available. No GraphFLA threshold-fraction calculation was run.

overlaps.graphfla_call: not run; no matching threshold-fraction output
overlaps.reason: No GraphFLA distribution statistic directly corresponds to these paper thresholds.

overlaps.locator: Figure 7 caption, panel d; Materials and Methods → “Paths between pairs of fit genotypes,” pp. 22–23
overlaps.quote: “Accessible paths are those that incorporate only fit genotypes.”; “The fraction of accessible shortest paths between two fit genotypes from data (orange) shows a modest decline as a function of Hamming distance.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “All genotypes one amino acid replacement apart are connected by an unweighted edge.”; “We next remove all vertices (genotypes) that are unfit, and recompute the number of shortest between the two parental genotypes.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The figure plots accessible shortest paths between fit endpoint pairs. The paper provides no printed numeric fraction, and GraphFLA global_optima_accessibility measures access to a global optimum on directed improving edges.

input.preprocessing: Figure 7 uses shortest paths between fit genotypes; no plot values were read and no GraphFLA path run was made.

overlaps.graphfla_call: not run; plot-only target and endpoint/path definition differ
overlaps.reason: The exact Figure 7 values are plot-only and were not read; the paper does not print an accessible-path fraction to reproduce.

blockers.what: Uniform-length segment genotype input for GraphFLA sequence landscape
blockers.why: The processed AAseq values have variable lengths; GraphFLA rejects the direct segment input before graph construction. No alignment, padding, or genotype filtering was applied.
blockers.needed_for: GraphFLA n_configs and any graph-derived metric on His3 segment 3

blockers.why: The downloaded processed tables contain amino-acid AAseq and fitness s; the supplementary workbook reports counts but the row-level nucleotide genotype-fitness table was not rebuilt or acquired.
blockers.needed_for: DNALandscape n_configs comparison to the printed nucleotide sequence counts

verdict_reason: The paper prints unique nucleotide and amino-acid genotype counts, site-level sign-epistasis fractions, model-fit R² values, and thresholded distribution fractions. A direct GraphFLA His3 build failed on variable-length AAseq input; the remaining candidates are definition-incompatible or, for evolvability_enhancing_mutations, unknown while the GraphFLA metric is under review. No local-optimum count is printed and no plot values were read.
